review:
Sleeping Dogs was originally going to be a direct sequel in the True Crime series many years before actually coming out. Thankfully, this never came to fruition. After a few changes, and a few publishers later, Sleeping Dogs came to be. Some will say it is the spiritual successor to the True Crime series. I'd like to think the connection never happened. Mainly because this game is just that good. Too good to be tied to a deservedly so dead series. 

Sleeping Dogs takes place in Hong Kong, and has you playing the role of an undercover cop with ties to a small group of triads, as you work your way up through the ranks, and work from both sides, as a straight up police officer, and an undercover officer playing a triad member who gets in too deep. It's a risky business, but for our main protagonist Wei Shen, it's all part of his life now. 

Sleeping Dogs is an open world action game modeled after games like Grand Theft Auto. You can run around freely, drive cars and ride motorcycles, and either take on main and side missions, or do other things as you progress through the game. Sadly, there is not much to do in terms of sandbox play. The world is very nicely detailed, and seems to be alive with the amount of people you will see moving about, but there just is not enough freedom to make this a real sandbox open world game. Most of the things you'll find yourself doing will be set up as part of the game instead. And anything you make up along the way will be few and far in between. Unlike open world games like San Andreas or Just Cause 2, where you can spend countless hours outside of any scripted events, making the game seem like your own little playground. This may be partially due to how constrained the world is. You can wander around streets, and inbetween buildings, and even inside of some, but the world is not as open as I would have liked it to be. Just don't be fooled by how big the map is, as lots of areas can not be accessed outside, due to barriers. Regardless, it is still a pretty big world. Just not ripe for exploration. Hopefully this gets remedied in the sequel. 

As for action gameplay, its nice. You won't find yourself using guns often, but when you do, the cover system is decent, and aiming is not too bad. You even get a few max payne style moves, like slo-mo diving thrown in the mix. The star of the combat however would be the hand to hand stuff, which is reminiscent of the Batman Arkham games. You will not be one on one most of the time, but rather one on many. Weaving in and out, doing parries, and a number of nicely animated kicks, punches, and grapples with ease. It's almost like poetry to see it in motion. When you are running from cops, or chasing down the enemy, you'll also find that Wei Shen is a good master of parkour. You don't have a jump button sadly to just jump whenever, but instead the parkour is tied to platforms and obstacles. So you run up to a wall, and Wei Shen will run up and grab a ledge when hit the proper button. He can jump over gaps, slide over obstacles like cars and tables, and more. Again, this is quite nice to see in action.

As for the audio, it's fantastic. You have a nice selection of radio stations, featuring both HK Eastern and Western themed stations, full of commercials, and great music. You also have some amazingly done voice acting, helping to bring the story to life, with a cast of seasoned voice actors and tv and movie stars. The voice acting is also a mix of english and cantonese. Mostly english spoken, but a bit of cantonese here and there for authenticity. Some characters will also only speak in cantonese. While pedestrians will almost always speak in english. But the accents are just right even when spoken in english. 

Sleeping Dogs may not be the ticket for anyone wanting a true sandbox open world game, but for those starving for a good action game with an open world set piece, and a great story. Sleeping Dogs is the perfect fix.

What was once shelved and left for dead by Activision is given new life and what would have been the third in the True Crime series is now Sleeping Dogs, exceeding expectations of just about everyone but Square Enix, the new publisher.

Sleeping Dogs was a game I bought in Steam's 2013 Autumn Sales, after being curious about this game for a long time and being aware that looking up YouTube footage might have spoiled the story for me, this sale was a good opportunity for me to just gamble on this one.

And it was jackpot for me. Having played Just Cause 2, GTA 1 to 4, Saints Row 3, L.A. Noire and countless other free roaming games, I was completely overwhelmed by how convincing Hong Kong was portrayed in Sleeping Dogs. Hong Kong, which in this review refers to the map in Sleeping Dogs, is a graphically pleasing platform that carries the player through a gritty storyline revolving around Chinese gangsters. Even though the city is small compared to most of the aforementioned free roaming city games, there is a healthy amount of detail put in every square foot of Hong Kong, making the city feel as big as it would have felt in real life. The city dynamics are downright convincing, you will encounter a large amount of variation among the residents, each with their own reason for being on the street. This, and the amounts of interaction provided for the player, is something that at the time of writing is not appreciated enough in the industry.

Sleeping Dogs features oriental themed music to reinforce that atmosphere. The genre of the background music as well as the radio stations vary from hip-hop to classic, all with Chinese roots. Luckily, a great majority of the used vocabulary is English, although you may encounter a Chinese swearword here and there. This is translated in the subtitles and may seem a bit forced, if not out of place. Personally I find it understandable considering a full English or Chinese transcript would've alienated the player from the casting in this context, or otherwise not being able to follow the story at all.

It's important that this appeals to the player as the emphasis of the game heavily lies on the implied Chinese gangster culture. This means that gunplay and car-craze is reduced to a minimum when compared to other games in this genre. Rather than mowing down your enemies it's more common to have to fight people barehanded, the use of several martial arts and enemies with different specialities makes this less linear than it may sound. I wouldn't go as far as calling this game less violent either, if anything, this game deserves its 18+ rating more than the others in its genre.

Having that said, the mechanics of the game definitely require getting used to, luckily this is achieved through a clever tutorial that gradually increases the freedom you have while playing.

To progress through the game there are countless of missions and events to participate in, and not all of these are fun to do. In fact, there's some dreadful shooter-on-rails included. Luckily this wasn't so common that it started to bother me more than I could take but these are things that make Sleeping Dogs far from perfect. It's a missed opportunity to go down in history as a classic, though looking back on what Sleeping Dogs did manage to achieve, it would be greedy to ask for much more. I already feel like a cheapskate having paid so little for what I got.

I greatly enjoyed playing Sleeping Dogs and within the 25 hours I needed to finish the story it has managed to claim a place on my list of all-time favourite games.

[IMPORTANT NOTE: I have played Sleeping Dogs on the highest settings and with HD textures (free DLC). This makes Hong Kong more crowded and makes everything look a lot better. I imagine this influences the experience quite a bit, so make sure to get the most out of your game.]

[h1] Overview [/h1]
[b]Sleeping Dogs[/b] is a third-person, open world action game [b]following the base concepts of GTA[/b], meaning a large city divided into sectors (all unlocked from the start), filled with main and side activities to take on and complete, each for different types of rewards. Unlike its bigger cousin, [b]Sleeping Dogs focuses more on melee combat rather than firearms[/b], featuring a [b]decently complex, satisfying, and really spectacular system[/b] that delivers the "martial arts action movie" feel almost flawlessly in each fight. Players will impersonate [b]undercover agent Wei Shun, and perform missions for both the Hong Kong police and Triads[/b], while trying to maintain their cover story. 

[b]The character development of Wei[/b] throughout the adventure is significant and [b]really shows how long-time undercover operations can make even paragons of the law become proper criminals, and why[/b]. Overall Sleeping Dogs is not completely realistic, as [b]it wants to convey an action movie feel rather than proper realism[/b], and does that very well, resulting [b]very enjoyable to play thanks to its variety[/b], featuring many types of side-missions ranging from drug raids, to races, to dates. This is a game I can [b]suggest to anyone liking martial arts action movies, crime stories, and also open-world action games in the style of GTA[/b] or Saints Row. 

[b]Reviewer's Note:[/b] [i]This review is for Sleeping Dogs Standard Edition + all DLC, so it is [u]equivalent[/u] to the Definitive edition.[/i]

[h1] Pros & Cons [/h1]

🔵 [b] Pros [/b]
+ Excellent open-world action gameplay, delivering good variety of activities with mostly meaningful rewards.
+ Interesting storyline, focusing on Wei's personal evolution, while depicting accurately the Hong Kong organized crime scene.
+ Spectacular melee combat system, varied enough and evolving thanks to several unlock-able moves and skills to use.
+ Overall great visuals and world detail, especially at night, impressive considering it came out in 2012.
+ With also DLCs and doing all side missions, expect around 25-30 hours of content, for the price you can find this game at around, is a very good deal.

🔴 [b] Cons [/b]
- Running around the streets like a muppet waiting for a Taxi (the only fast-travel method) to spawn is incredibly annoying.
- Race missions are generally too easy because of rather lackluster rival pilots' artificial intelligence. 
- Some side missions (like most Drug Busts) can be cheesed with vehicles to ram on-foot enemies, making them all trivial.
- Rarely, incorrect character spawns or AI behavior can cause mission failures. 


[h1] In-Depth Breakdown [/h1]


🎮 [b]Gameplay Analysis [/b]
The gameplay of [b]Sleeping Dogs[/b] is divided into Exploration, Main Missions, Side Activities and Combat.

[b]Exploration[/b] can be performed on foot or more easily using a vehicle, ranging from motorboats, to cars, trucks, motorbikes and so on, since almost every vehicle can be driven. Exploring Hong Kong thoroughly can deliver significant bonuses, first of all being Health Shrines, granting +10% max health every five of them found, invaluable later in the game. Lockboxes containing various amounts of money and unique clothes are also hidden in every nook and cranny, for completionists. Twelve statues unlocking powerful Kung Fu moves are scattered throughout the city, though mostly in noteworthy places. Aside from these collectibles, exploring can also lead to random world events, where some character will ask you to intervene in a situation, such as helping an escapee or driving out deadbeats. 

[b]Main Missions[/b] progress the storyline and divide into Triad or Police ones. The triad missions are about the ongoing war between the Sun On Yee sub-factions, while Police cases regard finding proof to arrest criminals or shut down illegal operations such as prostitution or drug trafficking. Generally, each Main mission has some unique gameplay factor to it, so none of them results boring or repetitive. Completing Main missions will grant large reputation bonuses based on the player's performance, granting Skill Points to spend in the respective skill tree (Face, Police and Triad), cash, and at some points unlocking Houses in each of the four city districts. 

[b]Side Activities[/b] are plentiful and worth doing. Favors are the most common, being side-quests for various characters, granting cash and Face reputation bonuses once completed, and generally are diverse enough to also not result repetitive. Drug Busts are also numerous, having player beat up dealers, then hack cameras in a logic mini-game, and finally have the dealer arrested, these are always the same and very boring at that, though, but also very rewarding. Races are divided in vehicle classes from C to A, purchasing a new vehicle class will unlock the relative races throughout the map.  Dates with girls are also worth doing because of powerful passive bonuses, such as ability to see Statues or Shrines on the map. Jobs are performed via phone contacts and are about getting debt money or stealing a specific type of car, then taking it back pristine, they pay out a lot of cash.

Last but not least, [b]Combat[/b] is one of the main gameplay features, proposing a fast-paced melee system with several mechanics to it, such as light and heavy attacks, combos having unique effects on enemies, grappling and throwing, counter-attacks, and disposable melee weapons from knives to batons lasting only a limited number of blows. The game will pit Wei against multiple enemies at once, using the environment cleverly, such as throwing enemies into air vents or down a cliff to instantly kill them, is an important mechanic. As the combat progresses, the Face meter will fill up, and once full unleash an adrenaline rush in Wei for a time, making his attacks more powerful, regenerating health, and granting unique bonuses based on the Face skill tree's level. Combat also features firearms but mostly later in the game: ranged fights play out as any cover-based shooter, headshots instantly killing anyone, and a decent variety of 10+ ranged weapons, but still nowhere near as good as the melee part, and feeling pretty generic. Car chases using firearms are quite spectacular though!


🔩 [b] Performance Analysis [/b]
The game has no performance problems to report and runs maxed out in 1440p and 144hz without issues. No crashes or severe technical bugs to note down. This is a fairly older game (2012) and will run well on low-mid spec systems in 1080p without too many issues or tweaks to make, thought for 1440p you may need some beefier specs to get a smooth performance with maxed settings. Compatibility with Windows 10 is good without issues in this regard as well. PC Specs: i7 4820K, GTX1080, 16GB RAM.


[h1] Final Thoughts [/h1]
[b]Sleeping Dogs[/b] is definitely a very good open-world crime action game, and is the closest thing to an "Asian GTA" around for the time being. Recommended to all who like action movies with a lot of fighting, martial arts, a good crime storyline, and open-world games with many side activities.

Sleeping Dogs is an open world action-adventure video game developed by United Front Games and Square Enix London. The game has you infiltrating the ranks of the Triads as undercover cop Wei Shen on an island off the mainland of Hong Kong.

A cover system is also included to allow you to avoid being shot and an interesting bullet-time mechanic allows you to vault over cover and take out enemies in slow-mo.

For those who like collecting stuff there is a large amount of collectable items in game to find while playing, you can also obtain several houses and dozens of clothing items, vehicles and furniture to customize your character. 

Sleeping Dogs also features achievements which cover all aspects of the game including DLC content so I suggest, if you care for the achievements, you also pick up the DLC so you can 100% the game. I took roughly 35-40 hours to 100% the game and should a Steam sale come up I think you should play it too!

INTRODUCTION:
Wei Shen a police officer trained in the USA, now working with the Hong Kong Police Department has been sent on a dangerous mission. To infiltrate and gather information on one of the largest and most dangerous Triad Organization in Hong Kong. Will he break under pressure or will he do his duty as one of Hong Kong's finest?

PROS:
+ Nice Graphics: -I like the visuals but you can clearly tell it was developed with consoles in mind. The only redeeming factor on this area is that a free high-texture DLC pack is available for download. The world is adequately populated by NPCs though at times some parts of the City does look empty. It has a day and night system as well as a weather system which adds to the game's atmosphere.

+ Expansive Map: -Though not geographically accurate to the real Hong Kong, the game still provides a massive Island to explore, populated by a number of NPC citizens as well as a number of drivable vehicles. Driving and exploration on this fictional representation of Hong Kong is very fun and oddly calming.

+ Interesting Combat: -The combat focuses primarily on punching people using street style Kung Fu martial arts, taking inspiration on the Batman Arkham games. Extremely violent and extremely satisfying in my opinion. This is further amplified by the fact that wearing different combination of clothing has benefits to your over all performance in hand-to-hand combat.

CONS:
- Very POOR Optimization: -As I said, this game was developed clearly with consoles in mind. Unexplained crashes, errors and FPS drops occur more than I would like. Not game breaking but It can be annoying and disruptive of the otherwise fluid gameplay.

- Story: -Though I found it interesting and fun, it's still rather predictable and rather cliche. Even going so far as to have one (or several), "The Godfather" moments. My primary complaint is that there is only one ending to this game and your choices never really affects the ending which makes both "Triad & Police points" a bit useless outside of the combat skill tree.

- Side Quest: -The game has a very good concept of side quest, offering both Police and Triad missions but they clearly weren't either finished or polished. I personally would have liked the "Drug Bust" missions to include proper detective work rather than have the game spoon feed who I should arrest.

CONCLUSION:
PRETTY GOOD. Notwithstanding the fact it's "like GTA", Sleeping Dogs is unique in it's own sense. The story has just the right feel to keep you interested and the gameplay offers enough action to keep you satisfied. Though it's current full price is good, I'd wait for a sale.

If you want a break from the fun and mindless violence of GTA, Sleeping Dogs can provide a fresh story based alternative.

Seriously though, this game is amazing.  It brings nothing particularly innovative or special to the genre of open-world-mayhem sandbox gaming, but what it does offer is high-quality, exciting gameplay and a well-written narrative. [b]Sleeping Dogs[/b] is a worthy pick-up for any fans of the genre looking for something new.

You can’t fly jets, grapple-hook atop buildings, drive a tank down a city street, or do some of the other extreme actions that are becoming common in the genre. [b]Sleeping Dogs[/b] is more grounded in reality and focuses more on having a believable narrative and atmosphere.  That said, the gameplay is still very enjoyable and there is plenty of extra stuff to do besides playing through the main story. Furthermore, the simple fact it takes place in Hong Kong goes a long way to add a little unique novelty  to the experience (like driving on the left side of the road, entering cars from the right, and just exploring a virtual city that isn't supposed to be in America for once).

It has a well-written story that is quite engaging and is reinforced with decent voice acting.  Combined with the nice graphics and atmospheric gameworld, it results in an excellent overall presentation. It definitely is an experience that feels more authentic than some of the more ridiculous games in the genre.   

I definitely recommend to any fan of the genre who is looking for some novelty that they check out this game.

Overview
Back in the days Sleeping Dogs should have been the counterpart to Grand Theft Auto.
Well Grand theft Auto is and will always remain a highlight. Especially in case of graphics, open world etc… but Sleeping Dogs confidents in his very own and special way.
 
You play an undercover police officer in Hong Kong, who tried to infiltrate the local triad. There you expect to collect tasks such as collect money, to fight other gangs, kidnap some important people, to steal cars etc. Soon you will experience that the Triad seek internal changes in the balance of their leadership. 
     
At the same time you are giving important information to your boss police). You take out some enemies before you can hack some surveillance cameras. With these cams you can watch drugs handovers, viewing the dealer and call the police to arrest him. You can also do some special missions, following some member of the triade, make hidden photos and listen to some discussions about money transfers.  
     
In my opinion, the story is very captivating and exciting. The voice acting is good and look very authentic. Dont forget, ist not america, ist hong kong, different driving sides, freakier cars and everything is like really densely built.
     
All quest are categorized in three different areas :
        
- Police Area (after completing a quest you earn xp and can level up)
     
- Triade Area (after completing a quest you earn xp and can level up)
     
- Social Area (after completing a quest you earn xp and can level up)
       
Many contents are comparable to Grand Theft Auto . There is a huge open world , lots of traffic , own cars (stealing, buying) , special clothing for your hero, weapons , several apartments and ancillary tasks. You can find hidden chests with money or clothing. To increase your energy, there are several shrines. To learn new fighting techniques, there are also hidden statues. These statues you can bring to your former teacher of martial arts. Afterwards he teaches you a new technique. You can train it in his fighting school. Focus of the game is the martial arts melee. Several kinds of enemies waiting for you :
         
- Light opponents
     
- Serious opponents
     
- Wrestler
     
- Enemies with weapons
     
- Covered Opponents
     
etc. 
     
 
In addition to the main tasks that you can solve, there will be also little Quests to raise your Social Status. For example helping a woman to sink her car in the river. With those points you can buy better clothes. The clothes also allow you to earn some extra attributes (for example 5 % more damage on enemies in fights). After some time you will have enough money to buy anything, it just matters how is your current level in each area (police, triade, social). Some things you can only buy if you have a minimum level in one of the areas.
     
    
Graphics
I dont want to talk much about the graphics. Check out some screenshots, even if you dont play this game on ultra settings, it looks great. It can not exceed GTA, but it still looks good enough in my opinion.
     
     
Controls
You can play it with both controller or keyboard. I prefer Keyboard, somehow I play most of those kind of games with mouse and keyboard. At least its much easier for me to hit targets with weapons instead of using the controller. 

      
My conclusion
If you like GTA, then you will like this for sure. You can feel the intensity of the main character. I really like his way he speaks, the way he acts. He fits totally for this job. 
       
If you love martial arts fightings with a mix of grand theft auto flavour, an open world, undercover action, a great story, then go and get it. I can only recommend the game.
     
Enjoy it

Sleeping Dogs was supposed to be part of the "True Crime" franchise but instead went solo after Square Enix bought the publishing rights. In my opinion, this game deserves way more recognition.

You play as Wei Shen, an undercover cop whose mission is to take down the Triads residing in Hong Kong. You'll uncover the power, corruption, secrets behind the gangs and know what it means to be Sun On Yee.

Story is a bit cliched in my opinion but is still very well executed. The character development is a bit weak, since I didn't actually feel any real, deep connections with the characters but the voice acting is honestly one of the best I've ever heard.

The visuals of this game is just wow, plus with the Hi-res texture pack, everything looks much clearer. Hong Kong is a bright vibrant place full of things to explore and people to kill. I live in a place where the environment is pretty much similar to Hong Kong so that's a plus xD I didn't really enjoy the music that much as you'll be focusing more on the action/driving/shooting.

The gameplay mechanics is the strongest point in Sleeping Dogs. It's like the Arkham series..... in an open-world-sandbox-type of game. Enemies are tough in the beginning, but you'll earn upgrades and moves that'll eventually make you untouchable ^_^ Guns are a rarity, since melee combat is its focus. Driving will take some time getting used to, it's very weird when you're driving slow and the camera angles don't really help, but when you're going fast, it's smooth and responsive.

Overall Experience: I love this game, but it could've been better. I've experienced lots of flaws in the game such as cutscenes  not loading, game crashing on startup, GPS keeps on redirecting me, cars launching to space etc. Despite all of these errors, the game is very well-made and is pretty solid for most of the time. Plus there are cameras to hack, hidden loots to find, altars to upgrade health, gangs to eliminate, statues to recover, songs to sing, toilets to piss in, people to kidnap and loads of other stuff to do in this game.... It'll keep you busy for hours xD I very much recommend this game especially if you love the open-world genre.

GTA Hong Kong. I believe this is the easiest way to sum up Sleeping Dogs. But it would also be incorrect as it gives you the impression that the game you are going to play will be exactly a GTA game but its setting will be a different city. That is why you should try Sleeping Dogs as it is so much more!

Gameplay-wise it is exactly what the newer GTA games are: you have an open world game where you go wherever you want and you can do whatever you want. Of course, doing some hit-and-runs will only anger local police so they'll be after you pretty quickly. You can approach icons scattered throughout the game that launch missions - those that are essential to the main story progress are indicated by a different icon than those who serve to be side missions only.

There are TONS of things to do in Hong Kong: you can participate in racing games, sing at karaoke parties, date girls, bet on cockfights, join a fight club. You also have hundreds of collectable items. It's worth participating in all these activities as the game rewards you with experience points that let you level up only to learn new abilities.

In GTA you you had an assortment of firearms available for you to use. Here, emphasis is on hand-to-hand combat. Learning new abilities makes martials arts even better. Carjacking is also available but can happen much faster than in GTA - you can jump into vehicles and there are also car chase sequences in the game.

Story-wise you play Wei Shen, an undercover cop, who climbs the criminal corporate ladder only to get closer to the bad guys he needs to expose. There are some nice surprises here and there and just like GTA this game can also steal around 40 to 50 hours from your life.

A highly recommended game if you liked GTA IV or any of its third-person shooter predecessors.

Sleeping Dogs isn't a game that does one thing perfect, but it's a game that does a lot of things incredibly well. The amount of effort that United Front Games put into development is shown from start to finish and the overall charm outshines that of any other sandbox game currently on the market. To help explain, the team spent weeks in Hong Kong taking pictures (20,000+) and recording audio to help their efforts in recreating the city. The world feels realistic and everything you encounter has personality. There was also extra work put into making it fully optimized for PC, fluid keyboard and mouse controls, specialized hardware support, and a day one high resolution texture pack to accommodate players with better machines are some of the few.

The game offers a nice mix of cop and Triad missions that help the pace of the overarching story, but there are plenty of things to keep you busy for the collector and completionist mind. Featuring a surprisingly well-driven narrative (... for a video game) centered around melee combat and parkour, there are also racing events, random jobs, fighting rings, hidden lockboxes, car deliveries, cockfights, gambling dens, dates (lol), and enough cars and clothes to collect to feel satisfied. Every character is fleshed out and feels real, the city is beautiful, and the soundtrack complements the themes and overall immersion very well.

After having owned the game since launch, it remains of one of the few that I still like to revisit every now and again. It's fun, it's cheap, and it deserves a spot in everyone's Steam library. Give it a shot if it's still sitting there with zero hours played and get hyped for Triad Wars.

Word of caution: You might be better off without the DLC for the first playthrough, as it gives you in-game experience that will unlock upgrades early on. It takes away most progression and is something to be wary of.

I rather enjoyed my playthrough of Sleeping Dogs, a Hong Kong set entry into the open-world crime genre. The undercover angle to the story also makes its way into the gameplay, encouraging you to balance violence and brutality to please the Triads with an adherence to law and order and minimized collateral damage to appease Wei’s police handlers.  It’s a great idea, but it really only comes into play during story missions.  Personally, I would have liked to see it expanded into other aspects of gameplay, especially the game’s side missions.

Further differentiating Sleeping Dogs from its neighbors is a focus on brawling over gunplay, which given the setting and story seems quite appropriate.  The fighting mechanics are accessible and I enjoyed opportunities to thrash hordes of thugs with little more than fists and whatever was around at the time.

Gameplay
This game plays like any other GTA like game, giving you freedom to roam around hong kong, although it focuses much less in weapon combat and much more in physical combat, and at any point in the game you either find yourself 

-- driving somewhere / Being chased / racing 
    This  isn't too bad as the driving in this game is surprisingly fun, the controls are a bit too fast on the turns and sometimes there are turns you really think you could make but can't for some reason. But the fun part comes from trying to not hit anything (the game rewards this), and drifting to try and achieve this. Also the mechanism of the hijacking moving vehicles is a fun take.
-- Fighting thugs
    The combat system in this game is not something out of this world and although it has some stiffness at times, it is mostly fluid allowing you to move from one combo to another pretty good, the main issue I see here is the enemy variety, although you get tougher enemies towards the end of the game, they play almost exactly the same as the beggining of the game.     Again as I have said before the story is what pulled me more into the game, and I find that the cutscenes are very well constructed and pull you into the game with them, immersing you into the story

Personal Notes

    I never really like when a game has a lot of collectibles to catch, I think the statues collectibles are a good kind of example where they are in kind of unmissable spots around the world and provide you with a good way to feel your character evolve, be it in the moves your character gains with them, or just the new location you've just visited to get that statue. But the other collectibles I feel don't add that much except just a need to get them all, and because they show up on the mini map they make me be glued to the mini map checking if any  of them appear.

    This is really a personal one, as I want to have 100% achievements in all games I play, so when a game makes me buy the DLC to get the 100% achievements it always leaves me a little bit mad
-- Humor
    The game has a great sense of humor and I found myself laughing quite often

I've heard this game reffered to as "a poor man's Grand Theft Auto". And while the moniker may come across as derogatory, I can't disagree. Certain aspects of Sleeping Dogs draw from open world titans like GTA, but it still manages to stand tall of its own merits, rather than on the coattails of GTA.

The pros are that it is a legitimately fun game to play. The story was interesting enough to keep me engaged and wanting to dig deeper, combat handled pretty well and was easy to learn, and a lot of the special actions you can perform, such as mid-driving carjacking, are pretty fun to pull off. The dual experience system is implemented fairly well, rewarding you for wreaking as much havok as you can upon your enemies, while punishing you for hurting, killing or destroying anything not related to your mission. Environmental hazards give combat a little more pep, allowing you to seriously injure, if not outright slaughter (sometimes quite brutally) anyone standing in your way.

The cons are that there isn't a terrible lot to do outside of the story quests, and what little there is to do becomes repetative and tedious with no meaningful reward. Some of the dialogue and situations/resolutions you come across can be pretty tongue-in-cheek if not outright absurd and cheesy, and felt detractive towards the overall tone and feel of the game. Combat, while easy to learn and diverse in what movesets you can punish your enemies with, ultimately boils down only attacking, grabbing or counters, and doesn't encourage making use of the many skills you can learn except for the sake of doing something flashy. NPCs will sometimes get stuck on terrain or on corners, making some missions impossible to complete without a restart.
But the two biggest offenders in this game for me, are the vehicle camera controls, and the option to purchase a number of game breaking features from the start through DLC content. The vehicle camera controls can be frustrating at best and damning at worst. It tends to lock itself in whatever position you move it to relative to your vehicle, and doesn't transition back to the forward position when you begin driving unless you move it back yourself, making multi-point turns and complex driving maneuvers aggrivating.
The DLC content almost broke the game for me at the start. I'll admit I grabbed the whole shabang without reading about it all when it was on sale, and I wish I had. After the first couple missions, I suddenly found myself awash in an inordinate amount of Cop and Triad XP, Face XP, money, vehicles and items.. enough so that what was supposed to be earned throughout the course of the game was instantly given to me at the start, making personal progression almost non-existant. If that's your sort of thing, then by all means. Otherwise be wary of what DLC you purchase.

Despite the cons and my own complaints about the game however, I'm left feeling quite positive about the overall experience. It's no GTA for sure, but I do think it's worth a look and a playthrough.

[h1][b]Full Review at [url=http://gamedragons.net/viewtopic.php?f=5&t=29]GameDragons.Net[/url][/b][/h1]

[b]Presentation[/b]
Originally developed under the title of True Crime: Hong Kong, what is now Sleeping Dogs is an open world action-adventure with the action set in the modern city of Hong Kong, in the middle of a conflict between two different parts of the controlling Triad, Sun On Yee. You play as Detective Wei Shen, an officer sent deep undercover to work for one side of the conflicted Triad Sun On Yee, controlled by the Red Pole Winston Chu. As you get the know the main cast, information about your past will be unveiled, revealing important information about Wei Shen's previous Triad encounters, as he grew up in Hong Kong alongside Jackie Ma, another one of Winston's soldiers. 

As an undercover cop you will spend most of your time working for different members of the Sun On Yee, constantly meeting new characters and increasing your reputation in the eyes of the Triad leaders. Apart from infiltrating the Triad gangs and doing missions for them, you can also spend your time in Hong Kong as a cop solving different cases that require a man on the inside to gather the information. There are only a few cases to solve and most of them are easily forgettable, but they're fun to do, plus they offer a whole new perspective of the game, allowing you to easily shift between the bad guy and the good guy. 

The story takes around 18 hours to complete, a journey filled with memorable characters and a plot worth following with a payoff that might be unexpected, yet surprising and satisfying, concluding with an ending that is open to interpretation, giving you the final verdict and decide what to do next in Hong Kong after completing the story. There is no doubt that the story is amazing in its own way, but believe it or not that isn't even half of the greatness this game brings, as you'll probably spend even more hours wandering around Hong Kong, completing favors, taking part in street races or looking for lockboxes and health shrines. Sleeping Dogs isn't the ultimate open world experience, but it certainly amazes in its own way, offering multiple ways to spend your time between missions, from playing games like Mahjong Poker to betting on cockfights or participating in fighting tournaments. 

[b]Gameplay[/b]
To whoever said there can be no further innovation on the current hardware, Sleeping Dogs is set to prove them wrong, big time; the amount of new and innovating mechanisms packed into Sleeping Dogs is quite surprising, introducing new ways to do things apparently simple, like picking a door or hacking a camera, creating a world in which almost every action in game requires a certain action on your side. There is so much to mention here, so only a few of the examples would be the bug calibration system that requires both analog sticks to be perfectly aligned with the environmental sound before plating the bug, or the camera hacking system that requires you to match the four digit code in order to access that camera. 

What is even more fantastic however, is the combat system, limiting shooting sequences to a few missions only, allowing you to concentrate on pure Kung-Fu melee combat; there are so many moves and combinations that make each encounter feel different, encouraging you to use every manoeuvre in your arsenal in order to defeat your enemies efficiently. The combat system allows you to interact with the environment too, as you can push your enemies towards a wall, smash their heads on the hood of a car or doing all sorts of things using the environment around you. In addition to your Kung-Fu moves, you can also use melee weapons like knives or hammers in combat, and disabling enemies using those to later use them yourself to your advantage. The shooting sequences are limited to only a few, yet they're satisfying and perfectly balanced with more Kung-Fu combats, creating an amazing and unique experience that no game could deliver before. 

There is also an experience system, which rewards you after each and every mission with experience points that will add up to a certain category, in which when you level up you can choose a new ability; completing missions for the Triads will award you Triad experience, while completing missions as a cop will award you cop experience, unlocking upgrades in a different category. In addition to Triad and Cop upgrades, you also earn Face experience for completing certain favours for random people you meet on the street, unlocking face upgrades that are this time more social oriented, offering things like reduced prices for cars or clothing. 

[b]Graphics[/b]
Sleeping Dogs isn't the most advanced game out there graphically speaking, but it's decent and it does a visual impression in its own way. The city of Hong Kong might not be as detailed as it could have been, but it's full of life and action, and that is what really matters. There is always something new to do in Hong Kong, and exploring the map is certainly one of them, as you'll sometimes be amazed of what you can find on the top of an unexplored building. 

The characters are beautiful and detailed, delivering that drop of personality they need in order to create an amazing and emerging story; the animations are amazingly done on the main cast, but even the secondary characters take advantage of some decent facial animations. There are some visual bugs however, like pedestrians walking inside the concrete, but it's easy to ignore those if you look a moment at how large and detailed the city of Hong Kong really is.

[b]Audio[/b]
Surprising enough, the mixture of Chinese and English in the dialogue works better than expected, delivering great and memorable lines that never cease to amaze. The cast of Sleeping Dogs includes some major names from Hollywood like Emma Stone in the role of Amanda Cartwright, James Hong as Uncle Po or Lucy Liu as Vivienne Lu. Will Yun Lee has been cast as Wei Shen, and needless to say, he delivered the lines with that special touch that made Wei Shen an instant classic character in video games. 

There are some lip sync issues that are hard not to observe, since they'll appear in the most important cutscenes in the game, but not in all of them. The soundtrack is simply amazing, always in the mood with the action, while keeping the atmosphere of Hong Kong with some classic songs that will make you shuffle through the radio channels just to listen to your favorite track one more time.

[b]Extras[/b]
You're looking at more than 25 hours of content, considering that the game doesn't end with the story, since there is an enormous world to explore and hundreds of items to collect. In addition to that, you can spend your time doing races, fighting in tournaments or replaying missions; it's like the game never gets boring as you always find something else to do, especially if you enjoy completing achievements/trophies, as some of them present quite a challenge.

[b]Verdict[/b]
Sleeping Dogs is without doubt one of the best releases of 2012 and a must have for any open world adventures fans, delivering a great story, innovating gameplay and an astonishing number of additional collectibles and extras. The game offers a superb experience worth playing, but most of all it proves that there are a lot of things that haven't been done with the current hardware before, finding its way into the top of the most innovating gameplay mechanics on the current generation.

[u]Rating: 9[/u]

Great and immersive game with a sandbox approach.  Graphics and sound are top notch and the main story line is engrossing!

Ultimately, I think Sleeping Dogs bites off more than it can chew.

It's tried very hard to be GTA IV while also being a Hong Kong action movie, and doesn't quite succeed. It starts off a bit like GTA but with kung fu instead of guns, and at first that's a lot of fun. Eventually, fistfighting becomes too easy - the melee system falls into the common trap of melee counters being a failproof tactic, and they're all-too-easy to pull off (just hold down the button, no timing necessary).

Being that this is trying to be GTA, they've thrown in a lot of driving, but it's not really very fun. It's far, far too easy. If you're on a motorcycle and you're going at anything less than full speed, you can have a head-on collision with a bus and the only damage will be the bus's fender; there's zero drawback to motorcycles but all the advantages of being able to cut through traffic. The risk vs reward is out of wack.

Gunplay is a bit lacklustre. There's a bullet time mechanic, but its inclusion is questionable. Wei Shen is a cop, not a super assassin, so why does he have the ability to slow time at will (but only during gun battles)?

As far as the story goes, things kind of turn to mush towards the the end. The whole "is Shen truly a cop or is he truly a Triad member?" thing feels a bit forced by the end. The opening bits with Winston and the Water Street Gang were great, but the quality of the plot disintegrates a bit towards the end. It feels like the writers started off strong but ran out of steam towards the end, and devolved into action movie cliches in order to wrap things up.

Various other bits and pieces seem to indicate that United Front simply tried to do too much. Shopfronts look awful, most of the animations are actually pretty crappy, camera controls are only just ok (I still have no idea what the camera was trying to do every time I reversed a car).

While a bit unsatisfying, I did have fun. Don't go in expecting very much and you'll probably be happy.

From the developers who brought you ModNation Racers, a kart racing game that makes Mario Kart seem unsuitably violent for children, comes Sleeping Dogs; the brutal, ultraviolent action game you've always anticipated would rise up gallantly, to try to compete with the popular GTA franchise, only to fall short by an unsurprising stretch. 

Not to say it's not an entertaining game, Sleeping Dogs reaches certain standards, most of all when it comes to innovating the field of satisfying your homicidal urges. After all, its progressive skill system is based on 'Face points’ that are awarded accordingly by how creative you are on your quest: to reduce the bodies of your enemies to the least identifiable shape possible (the important thing to know about evidence is that it’s best if there is none). You get the option to use the vibrant urban environment to your advantage, being given difficult choices like whether to crush all the bones in your opponents’ bodies with easily accessible car engines, or the equally effective maneuver of putting them gently down in a trash container.

The story is set in the metropolitan jungle of Hong Kong, and you have the privilege of following Wei Shen: the spiritual successor to every character Jackie Chan has ever played in films. He is an undercover cop and a master of martial arts before he even enrolls in the in-game martial arts class, and an unrelenting champion of doing the right thing. Like spending blood money on fancy clothes. 

Throughout Wei Shen’s journey, you will face difficult moral choices, encountering moments where you’ll have to decide whether a character or scene is merely stereotypical, inappropriately prejudice or straight up racist (for example: why it seems like every fighting individual seem to possess knowledge of, and skillfully demonstrates, advanced martial arts just because it’s set in Hong Kong).

You will be taken on an adventure where, as a servant of the law, you will rise in the ranks of organized crime through vicious acts, lie to near everyone you come across, and enthusiastically murder almost every goddamn person that stands in your way, be it suspects, gang members or policemen, and still getting to keep your job as a cop. Oh, and you also get the option of using prostitutes posing as masseurs for in-game bonuses, tasteful! An excellent social commentary on how the modern execution of justice is flawed and better handled by a single, unstoppable psychopath, who also enjoys karaoke.

Your toughest enemy throughout the game will be the agony of a typical, nightmarish PC port. You will be combating mortal enemies like painfully stiff controls and a swarm of bugs, along with strategically consistent game crashes to ultimately break your resolve. In addition, Square Enix’ support center seems to have lost all the passwords to all of their e-mails. A suitable challenge for only the most hardcore gamers, those who don’t really want to play at all. Final verdict: “it’s alright” out of 10.

You play as Rover, the friendly and intelligent family dog. Really now, you play as a Jackie Chan double who is actually a sleeper agent (hence the name, hurr durr) and you want no trabble. You fight your way through several ladder factories while holding several different babies, in your fight against slightly bigger asian people that look like they're straight out of Fast and Furious. You go through several losses, in this trainless society, and sleep with many prostitutes, although it is wisely disguised as if you are getting a massage from a massage parlour. You go through several girlfriends, and lose none of the perks that came with them after you pump and dump through all of them, essentially leaving the world with several Jackie Chan babies. You also learn many secret hidden techniques by picking up some sort of Chinese takeout food, or something along those lines, I don't really recall because it was unmemorable, but that's besides the point. The game has you fighting in a very enticing combat system that allows you to have fun while you steamroll everybody as if you were a train. A nicely curtailed, perfectly balanced open world game.  [i]Sleeping Dogs[/i] takes the very best of [i]Grand Theft Auto[/i], [i]Ubisoft Collect-a-thons[/i], and I'd guess [i]Yakuza[/i] (having only read about them) and distills it all down into a streamlined representation of the genre.  I really, really enjoyed my time with this game.  Wei Shen is a compelling character, the storyline is a hard boiled undercover cop story, replete with story beats you can see a mile coming, but performed so well I didn't care.  The emphasis on melee combat is the crowning jewel on what otherwise looks like a fairly superficial game at first glance.

I could have done without the "dates", the one-shot instances of Wei hooking up with various women he meets along the way.  It was a funny red herring when I noticed several big name actors in the opening credits, specifically Emma Stone, and assumed they'd have a prominent role in the story.  When Wei meets Amanda, a blonde American tourist, it was obvious she was voiced by Emma Stone and I rolled my eyes, thinking here would be our lame romantic interest that drives our hero.  Nope.  One interaction and she was outta here!

I did find the whole split XP system fatiguing, and spent the extra effort to swap out my outfits that provided Triad Bonus (for main missions) or Cop Bonus (everything else) just to reduce the likelihood I would need to replay missions to hit the achievement requirements.  It turned out not to be necessary.  The stat awards would a little irritating as well, but it did give me somethin to pay attention to while puttering around the open world grabbing the collectibles.  A word of warning: make sure to complete jobs that show up in the phone often.  I didn't realize that Tran's jobs were not infinite, nor required for 100%, so I had like 20 of them to crank through post-game.

DLCs were fun, especially the first [i]Nightmare in North Point[/i].  I suspect it was part of the zombie media craze going around in the early 2010s; gave me strong [i]Undead Nightmare[/i] vibes from [i]Red Dead Redemption[/i].  The second DLC [i]Year of the Snake[/i] was a pretty big disappointment.  It was fun seeing Wei adjust back to his life post-game, but the presentation and effort just felt off, like it was completed by a skeleton crew of developers.  The voice acting is way underplayed, the objectives are samey, and the big bad's motivation never felt fleshed out.  Oh well.

With the news that Square-Enix has sold off their Western IPs I'm hopeful we will get a sequel.  This game lives up to every bit of cult status it's built up over the years.  A strong recommend.
